objects.description: Opaque handle identifying a registered obs-websocket vendor. It is returned by obs_websocket_register_vendor and must be passed back to vendor API functions. Actual structure is hidden; treat as an opaque pointer.

Function pointer type for handling vendor requests. Signature: (obs_data_t *request_data, obs_data_t *response_data, void *priv_data). Implementations should read the request and populate the response object.

objects.definition: typedef void (*obs_websocket_event_callback_function)(uint64_t, const char *, const char *, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving obs-websocket events. Parameters are typically: timestamp (uint64_t), event vendor/name strings, and user priv_data. Exact semantics are not documented here.

Heap-allocated response container returned by obs_websocket_call_request. Contains HTTP-like status_code, optional human-readable comment, and response_data as a JSON string. Must be freed with obs_websocket_request_response_free.

Internal helper struct bundling a request callback function with its user data. Used when registering vendor requests. Not intended for long-term ownership by callers; stack-constructed and passed to the proc handler.
Internal helper struct bundling an event callback function with its user data for registration/unregistration. Not meant for persistent storage by callers.

functions.name: obs_websocket_get_api_version
functions.description: Return the obs-websocket API version provided by the loaded obs-websocket plugin. Intended for feature-gating and compatibility checks. If the obs-websocket proc handler is unavailable, returns 0. If the proc exists but the specific get_api_version call is missing (older plugin), returns 1.
requirements: obs-websocket plugin should be loaded; otherwise the function may return 0 (no handler) or 1 (very old API)
Caller should treat return values 0 or 1 as indicators that only legacy functionality may be available and gate usage accordingly
No arguments; safe to call repeatedly

functions.name: obs_websocket_call_request
functions.signature: static inline struct obs_websocket_request_response *obs_websocket_call_request(const char *request_type, obs_data_t *request_data);
functions.description: Invoke an obs-websocket request by name and return a heap-allocated response object that must be freed with obs_websocket_request_response_free(). request_data is serialized to JSON (via obs_data_get_json) and sent as the request payload. In C++ builds, request_data defaults to NULL.
requirements: request_type must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string naming a valid obs-websocket request (e.g., "GetVersion")
request_data may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid obs_data_t* suitable for JSON serialization
The returned pointer may be NULL if the obs-websocket proc handler is unavailable; caller must check for NULL before use
Caller must free the returned struct using obs_websocket_request_response_free() to avoid memory leaks
The response struct fields are: status_code (unsigned int), comment (char*, optional, freed by response_free), response_data (char*, JSON string, freed by response_free)

functions.name: obs_websocket_request_response_free
functions.description: Release all resources associated with a response returned by obs_websocket_call_request(), including the comment and response_data strings. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: response must either be NULL or a pointer previously returned by obs_websocket_call_request()
Do not double-free a response; call exactly once per successful obs_websocket_call_request() result
After this call, the response pointer and any of its fields must not be dereferenced

functions.name: obs_websocket_register_event_callback
functions.description: Register a callback to receive obs-websocket events. The callback will be invoked by obs-websocket with event metadata and the provided priv_data.
requirements: event_callback must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(uint64_t, const char *, const char *, void *)
priv_data may be NULL; it is passed back unmodified on each callback invocation
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates registration failed (e.g., obs-websocket not available)
The exact semantics of the callback parameters are not documented in this header; treat them as opaque event metadata

functions.name: obs_websocket_unregister_event_callback
functions.description: Unregister a previously registered obs-websocket event callback.
requirements: event_callback must be the same function pointer previously registered
priv_data should match the priv_data used at registration to unambiguously identify the callback to remove
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates unregistration failed (e.g., callback not found or obs-websocket not available)

functions.name: obs_websocket_register_vendor
functions.description: Register a new vendor namespace with obs-websocket and obtain a handle used for vendor-specific requests and events.
requirements: Must be called only from the obs_module_post_load() callback (explicit requirement in the header)
vendor_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string naming the vendor
Caller must check the returned handle; NULL indicates failure (e.g., obs-websocket not available)
The returned obs_websocket_vendor handle is required for subsequent vendor operations

functions.name: obs_websocket_vendor_register_request
functions.signature: static inline bool obs_websocket_vendor_register_request(obs_websocket_vendor vendor, const char *request_type, obs_websocket_request_callback_function request_callback, void *priv_data);
functions.description: Register a new vendor-scoped request type and its handler callback. When clients call this request via obs-websocket, the provided callback will be invoked.
requirements: vendor must be a valid handle returned by obs_websocket_register_vendor()
request_type must be a non-null, non-empty, NUL-terminated C string
request_callback must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(obs_data_t *, obs_data_t *, void *)
priv_data may be NULL; it will be provided to the callback
Caller must check the boolean return value; false indicates registration failed

functions.name: obs_websocket_vendor_unregister_request
functions.signature: static inline bool obs_websocket_vendor_unregister_request(obs_websocket_vendor vendor, const char *request_type);
functions.description: Unregister a previously registered vendor-scoped request type.
requirements: vendor must be a valid handle returned by obs_websocket_register_vendor()
request_type must be a non-null, non-empty, NUL-terminated C string naming a previously registered vendor request
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates unregistration failed

functions.name: obs_websocket_vendor_emit_event
functions.signature: static inline bool obs_websocket_vendor_emit_event(obs_websocket_vendor vendor, const char *event_name, obs_data_t *event_data);
functions.description: Emit a vendor-scoped event to obs-websocket listeners. The event_data pointer is passed through without altering its reference count.
requirements: vendor must be a valid handle returned by obs_websocket_register_vendor()
event_name must be a non-null, non-empty, NUL-terminated C string

event_data may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid obs_data_t*; the function does not modify its refcount, so the caller retains ownership and must ensure it remains valid for the duration of the call
Caller must check the boolean return; false indicates emission failed

data_types.description: A non-null, NUL-terminated ASCII/UTF-8 string used to name an RPC/request type or command. Typically consists of printable characters without embedded NULs; often alphanumeric with optional punctuation like dash or underscore (e.g., "GetVersion"). Empty strings are invalid for this use case.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a C identifier-like string used as request_type for
# obs_websocket_call_request. The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain
# this request string, defaulting to "GetVersion" when empty. Our goal is to
# provide valid, interesting request names that exercise different code paths.
#
# Constraints for request_type (from description):
# - Non-null, NUL-terminated C string
# - Non-empty
# - Printable ASCII/UTF-8, typically identifier-like
# Examples of known valid or likely-valid obs-websocket requests (v5 API):
#   GetVersion, GetStats, GetSceneList, GetCurrentScene, GetSourceTypesList,
#   GetInputKindList, GetInputList, GetStudioModeEnabled, GetRecordStatus,
#   GetStreamStatus, GetSceneCollectionList, GetProfileList, GetHotkeyList,
#   TriggerHotkeyByName, SetCurrentProgramScene, GetObsWebSocketVersion
# Include vendor-like names and edge-case names to expand coverage.

KNOWN_REQUESTS: List[str] = [
    "GetVersion",
    "GetObsWebSocketVersion",
    "GetStats",
    "GetStreamStatus",
    "GetRecordStatus",
    "GetInputKindList",
    "GetInputList",
    "GetSceneList",
    "GetSceneCollectionList",
    "GetProfileList",
    "GetStudioModeEnabled",
    "GetSourceTypesList",
    "GetHotkeyList",
    "TriggerHotkeyByName",
    "SetCurrentProgramScene",
    # Older API compatibility names (in case target maps them):
    "GetStreamingStatus",
    "GetRecordingStatus",
    # Vendor-style prefixes that some setups might register:
    "com.example.Ping",
    "plugin.vendor.CustomRequest",
]

# Character sets for composing identifier-like but varied names
ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits
SEP = ["_", "-", "."]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = [rng.choice(IDENT_START)]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        s.append(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT))
    return "".join(s)


def _rand_camel(rng: random.Random, words_min: int = 1, words_max: int = 4, prefix: str = "") -> str:
    words = []
    k = rng.randint(words_min, words_max)
    for i in range(k):
        wlen = rng.randint(2, 10)
        w = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        for _ in range(wlen - 1):
            w += rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
        words.append(w)
    base = "".join(words)
    return prefix + base


def _rand_namespaced(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce names like vendor.request or vendor.Sub.Request
    parts = []
    n = rng.randint(2, 4)
    for i in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, 2, 10))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_camel(rng, 1, 2))
    return ".".join(parts)


def _edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Edge but valid: max-length-ish, mixed separators, numeric tails, unicode ascii-range
    cases = []
    # Long but <= 255 bytes typical limit for names, keep modest to 128
    long_part = _rand_ident(rng, 32, 64)
    cases.append(long_part)
    cases.append(_rand_camel(rng, 1, 1, prefix="Get"))  # e.g., GetXxx
    cases.append(_rand_camel(rng, 2, 3, prefix="Set"))
    cases.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 8) + rng.choice(SEP) + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 8))
    cases.append(_rand_namespaced(rng))
    # Include dotted vendor with underscores
    cases.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 8) + "." + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 8) + "_" + _rand_ident(rng, 2, 6))
    # Include dash-separated
    cases.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 8) + "-" + _rand_ident(rng, 2, 6))
    # Include numeric suffix
    cases.append(_rand_camel(rng, 2, 3) + str(rng.randint(1, 9999)))
    return cases


def _choose_request(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weighted selection between known-good and synthesized names
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.55:
        return rng.choice(KNOWN_REQUESTS)
    elif roll < 0.85:
        # Construct common-style OBS request names
        prefixes = ["Get", "Set", "Create", "Remove", "Toggle", "Trigger", "Save", "Load", "Start", "Stop"]
        prefix = rng.choice(prefixes)
        return _rand_camel(rng, 1, 3, prefix=prefix)
    else:
        return rng.choice(_edge_cases(rng))


def _to_bytes_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure ASCII/UTF-8 encodable and no embedded NULs. Replace disallowed chars conservatively.
    s = s.replace("\x00", "_")
    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    # Append a terminating NUL as many fuzz harnesses pack raw buffers; FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # will typically read until NUL. Including NUL ensures clean C-string semantics.
    if not b or b[-1] != 0:
        b += b"\x00"
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    request = _choose_request(rng)
    # Keep under 4096 bytes; our strings are far shorter
    return _to_bytes_c_string(request)
